spec.name: Trend v9
spec.notes: Classic trend signal on trailing returns. Weekly rebalance.

claim.text: Research-period backtest: Sharpe 1.2, annual return 4%, maximum drawdown 7%.

exhibits.summary: Delaying the signal by 1 more bar moves the Sharpe ratio from 1.18 to 1.14 (change -0.03).
Under strict point-in-time data the Sharpe ratio moves from 1.18 to 1.18. Strict mode changed no field or operator the signal uses.
At 10 bps the Sharpe ratio is 1.12 (as submitted, 8 bps: 1.18); it breaks even at 48.0 bps with daily turnover 0.04.
On the full universe the Sharpe ratio is 1.18 against 1.18 as submitted; the strategy never saw 0 delisted assets.
On the sealed period, traded as live (strict data, 10 bps, at least one bar of lag), the Sharpe ratio is 0.14 against 1.18 in research, a gap of +1.03.
The best year gives 29% of total P&L (year 3) and calm regimes give 138%; Sharpe is 2.38 in calm and -0.92 in stressed regimes.
The log holds 333 distinct specs; the best of 333 under no edge is expected to reach a Sharpe of 0.89, so the claimed 1.20 becomes 0.31 and the probability that the true Sharpe is above zero is 82%.
The real signal's gross Sharpe of 1.41 beats 100% of 200 shuffled signals (shuffled mean -0.04, 95th percentile 0.57).
Perturbing the 2 numeric values in the signal by up to 50% moves the Sharpe ratio from 1.18 to as low as 0.50 (as low as 0.65 at 25%).
The top 1% of days (22 days) give 54% of total P&L and the top 5 assets give 30% (net of the strategy's own costs).

series.label: cumulative share of P&L, best days first
